# Choosing which sponsored listings to show

> Picks the highest-paying active campaigns with remaining budget today and returns up to 3 sponsored listings with signed click URLs.

_Part of [Sponsored ad campaigns and serving](sponsored-ad-campaigns.md)_

When a shopper views a product category, the `sponsored` method finds ads to show. It queries the database for all active campaigns in that category with products in stock, getting the top 10 sorted by cost-per-click. It then checks each campaign's spending so far today from [Daily campaign spend counter in Redis](daily-spend-counter.md), filtering out those that would exceed their daily budget. The top 3 eligible campaigns become sponsored listings—each gets a [signed click token](click-token.md) that encodes the campaign, product, and shop IDs plus a 30-minute expiry, so clicks can be attributed accurately.

**Look at:** [ads.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/application/ads.service.ts)

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | `AdCampaign table` | Read to fetch active campaigns in the category, their cost-per-click, and daily budget |
| database | `Product table` | Joined to fetch product title and verify inventory (quantity > 0) |
| cache | `Redis `adspend:{`campaignId`}:YYYY-MM-DD`` | Read to check each campaign's spending today against its daily budget; campaigns that can afford another click are kept |

## Watch out

- Budget check is approximate—uses Redis counters that may lag behind real spend if clicks are recorded asynchronously
- Fetches top 10 candidates then filters by budget, so fewer than 3 listings might be returned if many campaigns are budget-exhausted
- All three sponsored listings might be from the same shop if they have the highest bids in the category
- The token expires in 30 minutes (`TOKEN_TTL_MS`)—clicks older than that will be rejected, even if the campaign is still active
